body.statement: For a finite-dimensional linear program in standard form with rational constraint matrix, rational right-hand side, and rational objective, if the primal is feasible and has a finite optimum then the primal and dual optimal values coincide and rational optimal basic feasible solutions exist.  Feasible rational primal and dual points whose objective values differ by at most a prescribed positive rational tolerance therefore certify lower and upper bounds with that gap.

source.verbatim_statement: There is always a basic feasible solution and its bit complexity is not too large. If primal and dual are feasible, their values agree.

attestation.note: Lawful independent verification from MIT 6.854 Lecture 12: lines 8-9 establish an optimal basic feasible certificate with bounded bit complexity; lines 48-50 establish strong duality. For rational input, basic solutions are rational by solving the rational basis system. The cited Schrijver book metadata was confirmed in the author institution CWI repository.
